clue.text: It intrudes upon irrational thoughts, even given 10

indicators.note: the answer, the It of the clue, intrudes upon the two words, sitting inside them across the gap

explanation.surface: Something barges into a person's irrational thoughts, despite that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is the answer itself, which pushes into 'irrational thoughts'. 10 across is THAT, so the definition reads 'even given that'.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction means in spite of the fact that, a concession just like 'even given that'.

clue.text: In a stroke, Thu-Sun idol nails Ruddigore's opening and final act

indicators.note: the remaining pieces are placed inside the word for a stroke, splitting it

parts.note: a lash is a stroke of a whip

indicators.note: to nail is to pin something in place, so the joined pieces hold the single letter in their middle

parts.note: Thu is the standard short form of Thursday
Ra was the Egyptian sun god, an object of worship

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here the start of the operetta's name

explanation.surface: A long-weekend pop idol, mid-stroke, nails the start of Gilbert and Sullivan's Ruddigore and its finale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thu-Sun idol' reads as a long-weekend pop star, but it is two pieces: the day's abbreviation and the Egyptian sun god. Ruddigore is a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta.
explanation.definitionFit: A last hurrah is a final performance or effort before retirement, so it is a farewell act.

clue.text: Complex clue linked to an element of amino acid

indicators.note: complex means intricate or tangled, so the four letters of the word clue are jumbled

parts.note: In is the chemical symbol for indium, a chemical element

explanation.surface: A tricky clue tied to some component of an amino acid, as if a biochemistry puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' turns CLUE into LEUC, then indium's symbol follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Leucin, more often spelt with a final e, is one of the essential amino acids found in proteins.

clue.text: Tavern worker's snarling line is directed at twisted opera

parts.note: a bar is a tavern or pub

indicators.note: a snarl is a tangle, so snarling tangles the following letters into a new order

parts.note: a worker is a bee in crosswords, the worker bee; with the s it becomes bees
a gift for someone is directed at them, so for means directed at
a twisted mind is a wicked one, so twisted can mean evil

explanation.surface: A pub barman's growled remark is aimed at some warped opera he dislikes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snarling' tangles everything after the tavern into EROFSEVILLE; 'is' is only a link. The opera is Rossini's.
explanation.definitionFit: Rossini's comic opera of 1816 follows Figaro the barber, so the title names a famous stage work.

clue.text: Attending national army gathering as huntress

indicators.note: gathering means collecting in, so the first group of letters takes in the French phrase

parts.note: attending, as in at a party, gives at
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
the French phrase a la, as in a la carte, means in the manner of, so as

explanation.surface: Someone joins a gathering of the national army as a huntress, a woman among soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase sits just after the first two letters. The army is Britain's Territorial Army, its volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Atalanta was a swift virgin huntress who joined the Calydonian boar hunt.

clue.text: Supreme Creator of 4 missing in Independent

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the composer's name loses the following letters

parts.note: Rossini composed The Barber of Seville, the opera at 4 down
taken as written

explanation.surface: The ultimate creator of item four is absent from the Independent newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supreme' looks like an adjective for the Creator, but it names a singer from the Supremes; 'missing' strips IN and I from ROSSINI.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana Ross was the lead singer of the Supremes, the Motown girl group, so she was a Supreme.

clue.text: Like Maid Marian, are these Bristol City supporters showing off splendid breasts?

definitions.meaning: Maid Marian is the beloved of Robin Hood, so she is ..., belonging to Robin

definitions.text: are these Bristol City supporters showing off splendid breasts?
definitions.meaning: Bristol City football club is nicknamed after a red-breasted garden bird, whose fans wear its colours

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of football fans compared with Maid Marian, flaunting their chests.
explanation.definitionFit: Maid Marian belongs to Robin Hood, and Bristol City fans take the club's nickname from the red-breasted songbird.

clue.text: Break up — college holiday

parts.note: leave is time off work, a holiday

explanation.surface: A college vacation is when students break up for the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break up' pretends to be what schools do at term's end; here it means split.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave something is to split or sever it, as an axe does with a log.

clue.text: Variety of sea-life more diverse than a zoo

indicators.note: something more diverse is more varied, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: The ocean holds a wider range of creatures than any zoo could.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthozoa is the class of marine animals containing corals and sea anemones, a group of ocean creatures.

clue.text: Which is this guy's loosened tile?

indicators.note: loosened means freed of something, so the word this is set free of the possessive pronoun

parts.note: a guy's belongings are his
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A riddle asking which of these is the man's slipping hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' loosened of 'his' leaves only T. 'Which' is the relative pronoun, as in 'the book which I read'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are relative pronouns: 'the book that I read' and 'the book which I read' mean the same.

clue.text: Secret compartment (odd italics)

parts.note: a cab is the driver's compartment of a lorry or train

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of place, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hidden drawer described in strange slanted type, like a puzzle from a spy novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' turns ITALICS into ALISTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabalistic means having a secret or occult meaning, from the cabala, Jewish mystical lore.

clue.text: Fall in mutual back scratching terms

indicators.note: back means the remaining letters are read in reverse order
the terms of a phrase are its end letters; scratching them off leaves the run of letters inside

explanation.surface: Fall into a pact of mutual back-scratching, doing favours for each other.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the ends of 'in mutual' leaves NMUTUA, which 'back' turns round. 'Fall' is the American word for the season.
explanation.definitionFit: Fall is the North American name for the season between summer and winter.

clue.text: Chance it drove over one cutting kid's cake

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the inner letters split the biscuit word

parts.note: a rusk is a hard biscuit given to teething babies

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters of the past tense are read from right to left

parts.note: drove a car means ran it, so ran
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone drives over a child's cake, a reckless gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns RAN into NAR; with I it goes into RUSK.
explanation.definitionFit: To chance it is to take a gamble, the same idiom as exposing oneself to danger.

clue.text: Electoral reforms absorbing area budget again

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the shuffled letters take in the single letter
reforms means reshapes, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Electoral reforms that swallow up a regional budget, a dry political headline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforms' rearranges ELECTORAL and 'absorbing' takes in A.
explanation.definitionFit: To reallocate funds is to divide them up afresh, assigning a fresh distribution of money.

clue.text: Tea? You might pay me to do some fish

definitions.meaning: British slang for tea, from the Chinese word cha

definitions.text: You might pay me to do some
definitions.meaning: a ..., or charwoman, is a hired cleaner paid to do some housework
a fish of the trout family found in cold lakes

explanation.surface: A cafe worker offering tea and offering to prepare some fish for a fee.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: a charwoman is a paid house cleaner in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Char means tea in British slang, a hired cleaner, and a trout-like fish.

clue.text: Below ground fireman's cut me loose

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are rearranged
cut and loose together say the small word is let go from the jumble
set loose means freed, so those letters leave the mix

parts.note: the word fireman, its possessive s read as has

explanation.surface: A fireman underground frees someone trapped below.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix FIREMAN with ME taken out ('cut me loose'), then rearrange ('ground').
explanation.definitionFit: Infra is Latin for beneath, used in English as in 'see infra', meaning see further down.

clue.text: To dedicate to pirate is cutting in itself

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the word for pirate goes into the Latin phrase

parts.note: in se is Latin for in itself
to crib is to copy someone else's work, as a pirate copies

explanation.surface: Dedicating something to a pirate is itself a cutting act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in itself' is the Latin phrase IN SE, which CRIB cuts into; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To inscribe a book is to write a dedication in it to someone.

clue.text: Cunning opening

definitions.meaning: ... means sly or knowing, as in an ... smile
a curved opening, such as an archway

explanation.definitionFit: Arch means slyly knowing, and an arch is a curved doorway or passage.

clue.text: Writer's in wreck of car left on perimeter fence?

indicators.note: placed on the perimeter means set around the edge, so these letters go round the others
a wreck is something smashed up, so the letters of car are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
the writer is the setter, so writer's means I am, I'M
taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer is inside a crashed car left on the perimeter fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wreck of' gives CRA. 'perimeter fence' looks like a barrier, but 'on perimeter' is the container signal and a fence here is a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence is slang for a dealer in stolen goods, so a lawbreaker; the question mark flags the double meaning.

clue.text: Do mid-morning break three hours early, say, and swap tips

indicators.note: to swap is to exchange, so the second end letter changes places too
the tips are the end letters of the word, and the leading one goes to the far end
three hours earlier than eleven is eight, so the hour in the name changes

parts.note: elevenses is a British mid-morning snack break, named after eleven o'clock

explanation.surface: Take an early coffee break, three hours ahead of schedule, and trade advice.
explanation.walkthrough: Elevenses is a British mid-morning snack. Moved three hours early it becomes a made-up 'eightses' ('say' admits the coinage); 'swap tips' exchanges its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To do a city, as a tourist, means touring its sights.

clue.text: Just like the rascal one is, jumping ship

parts.note: one is, said of oneself, becomes I am, shortened to I'M

indicators.note: jumping means leaping about, so the letters of ship are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rascal deserting his vessel, like one who jumps ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumping' turns SHIP into PISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Impish means mischievous, behaving like an imp, a little rascal.

clue.text: Time you need to take on lush picture

parts.note: a lush is a heavy drinker, an alkie

explanation.surface: You must spend time taking on a drunk in your picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A talkie was an early film with sound, and a picture is an old word for a film.

clue.text: Hats off to Juno, collecting herself overseas sovereignty

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so the two initials hold the goddess between them
the hats of words are their tops, their first letters, taken off them

parts.note: Juno's Greek counterpart, the same goddess abroad, is Hera

explanation.surface: A salute to the goddess Juno, gathering her own empire across the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman Juno is the Greek Hera, the same goddess 'overseas'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Raj was British sovereign rule over India, from the Hindi word for reign.

clue.text: Pest destructively set about exposed cuticle

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the rest
destructively means wrecking, so the three letters of set are jumbled
exposed means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters are removed

parts.note: the cuticle is the epidermis, the outer layer of skin

explanation.surface: A pest attacks bare cuticles, like a skin-damaging parasite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destructively' makes STE from SET, and 'exposed' strips the ends of EPIDERMIS, leaving PIDERMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Spider mites are tiny arachnids that infest plants and damage leaves, a garden scourge.

clue.text: Like this will cost me my treasure!

definitions.meaning: expensive, so something this way costs a lot
a term of affection for a beloved person

explanation.surface: Someone muses that this will be expensive, my precious.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear means costly and is also a fond term for a beloved person.

clue.text: Yellow's out of range with it

indicators.note: out of means taken away, so the word for range is removed

parts.note: yellow means cowardly, as is chicken
ken is range of knowledge, as in beyond my ken

explanation.surface: A yellow colour is beyond the range of what is fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yellow' looks like a colour, but it means cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish and fashionable, the same as being trendy.

clue.text: One partner of Oliver H's caught drunk in French city

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the 's reads as has, and has caught means holds inside

parts.note: Oliver Hardy's comedy partner was Stan Laurel, so by the same style Stan L
bu is the French past participle of boire, to drink

explanation.surface: One of a comedy double act gets caught drunk in a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver H(ardy) pairs with Stan L(aurel), shortened the same way. The surface suggests a French city, but the definition is just 'city'.
explanation.definitionFit: Istanbul is the largest city in Turkey, formerly Constantinople.

clue.text: Rail service vehicle in which to race the old girl westward

indicators.note: in an across clue westward means read from right to left

parts.note: a kart is a small racing car
the old girl is mother, MA

explanation.surface: Racing your mother westward in a vehicle, cross-country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'westward' turns KARTMA round.
explanation.definitionFit: Amtrak is the American national passenger railroad company.
